sources_considered.why: Primary evaluation of object and spatial consistency in image generation.
Primary experiments on multistep compositional reasoning.
Primary evidence of increased training data, refinement, and improved but imperfect performance.
Contemporary primary acknowledgement of factual and reasoning errors, together with improvements.

evidence_items.explanation: The evaluation reports substantial failures to generate requested object relationships despite strong visual quality. This supports difficulties with spatial world consistency, without proving the absence of internal world models.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract; experimental details checked in sections 3.1 and B.1 of the full paper
evidence_items.explanation: Experiments on multiplication, logic puzzles, and dynamic programming document sharply worsening performance with task complexity. These are repeatable multistep reasoning difficulties, rather than isolated anecdotes.

evidence_items.locator: Appendix A.4.8; training changes in sections 1–2; limitations in section 5.2
evidence_items.explanation: The report documents 40% more pretraining tokens, revised data selection, and remaining hallucination risks. It also reports improvements, which limit any interpretation that greater scale or refinement brought no benefit.
OpenAI acknowledges continuing factual and reasoning errors in GPT-4. The same section reports improved factuality relative to GPT-3.5, showing that persistent limitations coexisted with progress.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not provide one representative failure rate covering all generative AI.
No controlled comparison isolates training-data growth across all three capability areas.
Spatial generation tests cover only part of what world modeling can mean.
